summary: Defines the EDIINT-Features header field, which lets EDIINT applications (AS1, AS2, AS3) announce optional features they support. This helps avoid problems when a partner does not support a feature. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: EDIINT systems can have different optional features. This RFC defines a header that tells a trading partner which features the sending user agent can support.

questions: what does the ediint-features header do
which characters can a feature name contain
subtitle: A header field lets EDIINT user agents announce the features they can support.

tldr.problem: EDIINT applications can support features beyond basic transport, but trading partners may not support the same features.
tldr.mechanism: The EDIINT-Features header lists feature names and must appear in all messages sent by the user agent.
tldr.outcome: Partners can see declared capabilities without prior out-of-band agreement; RFC 6017 is Informational.

today: RFC 6017 is an Informational document. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Announcing EDIINT Features
sections.content:
EDIINT applications provide secure transport for payload documents. As AS1, AS2 and AS3 developed, applications added features beyond the basic transport function, and not every implementation supports every feature.

The EDIINT-Features header lets an originating user agent tell its trading partner which listed features it can support, without out-of-band communication and agreement.
sections.plainLanguage: The sender lists supported features in a message. The partner can use the list when deciding which features to use.

sections.title: Header Syntax and Processing
sections.content:
The header contains one or more comma-separated feature names. A feature name uses letters, digits and hyphens, and names are case-insensitive. The field may appear in an AS1, AS2 or AS3 message.

The header must be present in all messages sent by the user agent, not only messages that use a feature. A trading partner should assume the user agent can receive messages using the listed features. Any feature using this field must be specified in an RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: Feature names form a comma-separated list. The sending agent includes the list on every message, even when it does not use those features.

sections.title: Version Headers and Security
sections.content:
AS2 and AS3 use version headers. An implementation supporting EDIINT-Features must use version value 1.2; this version builds on 1.1, which indicates compression support. Therefore an AS2 or AS3 implementation at version 1.2 must support compression even if the feature is not listed.

AS1 has no version header. Partners that have not implemented EDIINT-Features can ignore the field. The RFC warns that headers may be unencrypted and could be altered; partners may confirm feature support out of band.
sections.plainLanguage: AS2 and AS3 use version 1.2 to signal support for this header, and that version also requires compression support. Unencrypted headers may be altered.
